header.name: Digital Signal Processing
header.description: Digital signal processing has rapidly developed over a past few decades due to significant developments in digital computer technology. This course develops on the foundations of the pe-requisite course on “Signals and Systems.” In this course, students are introduced to the basic analysis tools and techniques for the processing of digital signals. The course deals with the conversion of analog to digital signals, Fourier domain approach for the analysis of discrete-time signals and systems, design of filters, and introduction to multirate digital systems.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Analyze discrete time systems in time domain, z domain and frequency domain

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Analyze and implement digital systems using DFT and FFT

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Realize digital filters using different structures

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Apply design techniques for digital filters according to specifications

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Use Python for analysis and design of DSP systems

lecture_topics: Digital filtering: Block diagram, signal flow graph representation
structures of IIR and FIR filters (direct, cascade, parallel, feedback, lattice, lattice-ladder structures)
LTI systems: Phase and group delays
Digital filter design - Finite impulse response (FIR) filters: [1] Window design techniques, Kaiser window design technique, Equiripple approximations
Infinite impulse response (IIR) filters - Bilinear transform method

resources.title: Digital Signal Processing: A Computer-Based Approach, S. K. Mitra, McGraw-Hill, Third edition, 2006.
Digital Signal Processing by John Proakis & D. G. Manolakis, 4/E. Pearson, 2006.
Discrete-Time Signal Processing, A. Oppenheim and R. Schafer, Prentice Hall, Second edition, 1999
